A SCORE, NOT A SHARE

What does 67 out of 100 mean?

It means the three questions for that tendency produced a rounded score of 67 using our calculation. It does not mean “67% of your personality,” “more than 67% of people,” or a 67% chance of having a particular trait.

Each tendency has its own scale. Your seven scores can total more than 100 or less than 100 because they are not pieces of a single whole. Treat the chart as seven readings beside each other, rather than slices of a pie.

Higher means more agreement with these items.

After balancing statements are reverse-scored, a higher number means the situations chosen for that tendency matched more closely. The quiz does not set validated low, medium, or high thresholds. See the calculation.

NO TIE-BREAKING TRICKS

Equal scores deserve equal billing.

Two or more tendencies can share the highest score. The result lists every leader instead of using alphabetical order or a hidden rule to choose one. If all seven match, the result becomes an Even Ensemble.

Small differences also deserve proportion. Each tendency has only three questions and a raw total out of 12. A one-point change in that total is about 8.33 points on the displayed scale. A score of 75 beside 83 can therefore be one raw point apart, rather than evidence of a large personality difference.

All-zero scores and all-100 scores also produce evenly matched profiles. Neither establishes a moral ranking or makes the test a measure of virtue.

A USEFUL WAY TO READ IT

Start with a moment,
not a label.

  1. Read the full profile.Notice the other six scores as well as the leading character. A single headline leaves out part of your answers.
  2. Find one recognizable situation.Think about an actual message, task, purchase, or comparison. Ask what was happening around it.
  3. Choose one small reflection.The character guides offer prompts and optional experiments. Use what is relevant rather than treating the result as an instruction.

Explore the seven-character overview to choose a guide. Retaking the quiz can produce different answers at a different time; changes are not a validated measure of improvement or decline.

YOU CHOOSE WHAT TO SHARE

A character card and a result link
share different things.

The downloadable PNG shows your leading character or characters without the numerical score chart. The result link includes all seven scores after the # in the address. Anyone with that link can view the profile.

The example links on this guide contain only illustrative scores. A link copied from your own result contains your scores. You can also share the quiz itself without sharing a profile.

GOOD QUESTIONS

Before you overread the chart.

Why are my scores not percentages of one total?

Each scale has its own three questions and denominator of 12. Converting each scale to 0–100 makes them easy to display together; it does not make them shares of one total.

Can I compare my score with a friend’s?

You can compare the situations you recognized and use the profiles as a conversation starter. The quiz has no representative comparison group, so a numerical difference does not establish a reliable difference in personality.

Why did I get a different result this time?

Changing an answer can change a score. Your interpretation of a situation or the context you have in mind may also change. This quiz has not established test–retest reliability, so it cannot tell you what a score change means.

Does a low score prove I do not have that tendency?

No. A low score means these three statements fit less closely. It cannot establish how you respond in every situation.
